title: Dissecting pleiotropy between major depressive disorder and physical disease comorbidities.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the supplementary workbook (41588_2026_2735_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx, 56 sheets) and counted rows: the four locus tables hold 172 (cardiovascular), 537 (metabolic), 170 (gastrointestinal) and 140 (immune) independent loci, exactly matching Supplementary Table 14. Pulled the figshare readme and the first 8,287 lines of MDD_Immune_Factor_withQSNP.tsv.gz by ranged GET: tab-separated, header CHR BP A1 A2 beta SE MAF P SNP Z, genome build GRCh37, parsed cleanly. Confirmed the figshare record is public CC BY 4.0 with 8 files of 227-318 MB each, and that the Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.21711189) is analysis code only, no data.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The genomic structural equation model itself (how the four disease factors and the shared MDD liability were defined), the QSNP heterogeneity filter that removes variants not acting through the factor, the 47% heritability figure, and the per-factor effective sample sizes (826,320-926,436). I did not download any full summary-statistics file, so the 6.47-6.86 million SNP totals per factor come from Supplementary Table 14, not from counting lines.

a1_downloadable.note: figshare record 32916761 is open, CC BY 4.0, no login; I pulled bytes from one file directly. Verified in the files. (The multiple sclerosis input GWAS is request-only, but that is an input to their model, not the released product.)

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Per-variant effect on each disease-MDD factor is literally a column (beta, SE, P, Z) in the released tables. Verified in the file header and first rows.

a3_inputs_present.note: Borderline. The files contain NO features at all - only rsID, chromosome, position, alleles and allele frequency. Every predictor (reference DNA sequence, annotation tracks, linkage-disequilibrium panel) must come from elsewhere; coordinates plus the stated GRCh37 build make that a bulk script rather than thousands of lookups, so it passes narrowly.

a4_units_stated.note: readme.txt on figshare names every column and its unit (beta = SNP effect, SE, minor allele frequency, P, Z) and the genome build. Verified by reading the readme.

a5_enough_rows.note: 6.5-6.9 million variant rows per factor, but variants in linkage disequilibrium are not independent; the honest unit is the locus (172+537+170+140 = 1,019 significant loci, verified by counting) or the ~1,700 standard European linkage-disequilibrium blocks. Passes, but only just, and 6.8M is misleading.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Each gzipped file is 227-318 MB (verified on figshare), roughly 1.5-2.5 GB uncompressed; one factor at a time, or a HapMap3 variant subset, streams fine in 16 GB RAM. All eight files plus a reference genome would exceed the project's comfort zone.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Loci counts in the four locus tables (172/537/170/140) match Supplementary Table 14 exactly, counted in the workbook. Per-variant totals not independently counted.

a8_label_provenance.note: Conditional pass with a loud warning. The label is not another machine-learning model's output, but it is a latent-factor estimate produced by genomic structural equation modelling - a weighted combination of 20+ published disease GWAS plus the MDD GWAS. So the label is exactly reconstructible from public data that would be the most natural features; only a strictly sequence-based project avoids leakage by construction.

B1.why: Eight separate genome-wide files plus a 56-sheet workbook; they join on rsID and coordinates. Seen in files.

B2.why: Gzipped tab-separated with a header row; parsed on first try from a ranged GET.

B3.why: All four factor files are on the same standardised genomic-SEM scale, produced by one pipeline. Verified in readme and headers.

B4.why: No censored or qualitative values in the columns I read; beta, SE, P, Z all numeric.

B5.why: One row per variant per factor in the partial file I read; no duplicate rsIDs in the first 8,287 lines.

B6.why: readme.txt documents every column and the genome build; workbook has a table of contents for all 56 sheets.

C1.why: A sequence-only test of whether foundation models see pleiotropic loci is informative either way, but a negative is the expected result.

C2.why: PLEIO, PolarMorphism, FactorGo, Open Targets locus-to-gene all exist and are open; retrieved their papers, not guessed.

C3.why: Angle is weak: the factor statistics are new objects, but the task is the crowded sequence-to-GWAS-signal problem.

C4.why: The current method (genomic SEM on public summary statistics) is already cheap and runs in hours; nothing slow to replace.

C5.why: No published predictive number to beat; only dummy baselines (allele frequency, gene density) and locus-to-gene scores.

D1.why: Nucleotide Transformer, DNABERT-2, AlphaGenome all match DNA at GRCh37/38 coordinates; open or released weights.

D2.why: Embedding ~1,000 loci on CPU is fine, but any per-variant genome-wide task needs a GPU; paper text plus my own experience.

D3.why: Data is CC BY 4.0 (verified on figshare), but AlphaGenome weights are non-commercial; DNABERT-2 is permissive.

E1.why: Hold out whole chromosomes or standard linkage-disequilibrium blocks; coordinates present in files.

E2.why: 22 chromosomes and ~1,700 European linkage-disequilibrium blocks available as held-out groups.

E3.why: Dummy baselines computable: minor allele frequency, distance to nearest gene, local variant density.

E4.why: No replicate measurement of the factor statistic; standard errors are model-based, not independent repeats.

E5.why: Positive control available: the major histocompatibility complex region must light up for the immune factor.

E6.why: Label shuffling within linkage-disequilibrium blocks and feature ablation both runnable on this table.

E7.why: The with-QSNP and without-QSNP versions, plus any independent disease GWAS, give a second source.

E8.why: No published predictive performance number on these factors exists to reproduce; only association statistics.

G1.why: rsID plus GRCh37 chromosome and position in every row, verified in the file header.

G2.why: Open Targets, GTEx and the AlphaGenome variant-effect atlas all join on coordinates or rsID.

G3.why: Coordinate joins need GRCh37-to-GRCh38 liftover and multi-allelic handling; manageable but not one-to-one.

G4.why: Combination asks whether regulatory predictions separate gut-brain from metabolic loci; stratified heritability already answers much of it.

H1.why: Negatives exist as non-significant variants, but their status reflects statistical power, not biology.

H2.why: European ancestry only throughout; Supplementary Table 1 lists exclusively European-ancestry input GWAS.

H3.why: The honest claim is writable in one sentence; see honest_claim_h3 field.

H4.why: Ancestry restriction and QSNP filtering are explicit in the paper and supplementary tables.

I1.why: Psychiatric genetics groups (QIMR Berghofer, Psychiatric Genomics Consortium) and gut-brain researchers would read it.

I2.why: A sequence model's ranking of these loci would not redirect any experiment they are currently planning.

I3.why: Metric would be ranking quality, but the real decision is which gene to assay, which this data does not label.

I4.why: Simple rules (allele frequency, gene density, open-chromatin overlap) likely match any model on ~1,000 loci.

J1.why: Real splits and transfer learning involved, but most time goes to genome-scale data wrangling.

J2.why: Statistical-genetics intuition needed to tell a real signal from a power artefact; not a domain I could self-check easily.

J3.why: A tidied locus table is shareable, but the headline claim needs the full modelling to mean anything.

J4.why: No time budget defined; the liftover and linkage-disequilibrium plumbing makes the estimate vague.

J5.why: No kill date written; nothing in NOTES.md for this candidate.

existing_models.name: Genomic SEM (this paper's own method, structural equation modelling of GWAS summary statistics)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a predictor; reports model fit (comparative fit index 0.918, standardised root mean residual 0.055 for the four-factor model, read in Supplementary Table 3). No held-out predictive number exists.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Causal direction between MDD and the gastrointestinal factor, and which genes at the shared loci are causal, both remain unresolved in their discussion.

existing_models.name: PLEIO (Pleiotropic Locus Exploration and Interpretation using Optimal test)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published in American Journal of Human Genetics as an association test, not a predictor; evaluated by power simulations rather than a train/test split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Interpreting which trait drives a pleiotropic signal at a given locus.

existing_models.name: PolarMorphism (shared-variant discovery from GWAS summary statistics, Bioinformatics)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reports discovery of shared variants across trait pairs; no held-out predictive metric.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Extension beyond pairs of traits and handling of sample overlap.

existing_models.name: FactorGo (variational factor analysis of biobank GWAS summary statistics)
existing_models.score_and_split: Estimated 100 latent pleiotropic factors across 2,483 phenotypes; evaluated by simulation and factor interpretability, not prediction.

existing_models.name: Open Targets Locus-to-Gene (L2G), gradient-boosting model, Nature Genetics 2021
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 445 gold-standard curated GWAS loci with nested cross-validation; outperforms a distance-only baseline; score is calibrated as the fraction of gold-standard positives.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Causal gene assignment at loci without colocalising molecular QTL evidence.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or DNABERT-2 (DNA language models) on GRCh37 windows around lead variants; AlphaGenome as an alternative regulatory-effect feature source
backbone.hardware: CPU for ~1,000 locus windows; a GPU for anything genome-wide
backbone.licence: DNABERT-2 permissive; AlphaGenome weights non-commercial; the data itself is CC BY 4.0

integration.partner_dataset: Open Targets Platform (gene-disease-drug evidence) and the AlphaGenome precomputed variant-effect atlas
integration.join_key: rsID, or chromosome and base position after GRCh37-to-GRCh38 liftover
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do predicted regulatory effects distinguish the loci shared between depression and gut disease from those shared with metabolic disease, pointing at different tissues of origin?

controls.positive_control: The major histocompatibility complex region on chromosome 6 must rank near the top for the immune-MDD factor; any pipeline that misses it is broken.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the factor statistic within linkage-disequilibrium blocks and confirm performance collapses to the allele-frequency baseline.
controls.external_validation: The with-QSNP versus without-QSNP file pairs, and any independently published disease GWAS not used in their factor model.

honest_claim_h3: A sequence-based model could at best claim: among European-ancestry variants that reached genome-wide significance for a statistically derived depression-plus-physical-disease liability factor, DNA sequence context ranks them better (or no better) than allele frequency and gene density - a claim about the output of one structural equation model, not about disease biology.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence around each variant to predict its effect on shared depression-plus-physical-disease genetic liability.
plain_idea.train_on: A window of reference DNA sequence around each variant, embedded by a DNA language model. Verified counts: 1,019 genome-wide-significant loci across four disease factors, drawn from 6.5-6.9 million variant rows per factor.
plain_idea.predict: The variant's effect size (beta) or Z statistic on one of four latent depression-disease factors. The true answer is not a direct measurement: it is an estimate from genomic structural equation modelling applied to 20+ published case-control GWAS plus a depression GWAS.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Psychiatric genetics groups studying the gut-brain axis would want to know whether sequence context separates gut-shared from metabolism-shared depression loci; a clear negative would also usefully document that DNA foundation models add nothing over allele frequency here.

more_or_better_data.why: Open Targets locus-to-gene was trained on 445 curated loci but is applied across all published GWAS; FactorGo used 2,483 phenotypes. This paper contributes 1,019 loci from 4 factors built on European-ancestry data only - smaller and narrower, not bigger.

confidence_score.why: Standard errors are in every row, so prediction intervals are expressible, but those errors are model-based (from the structural equation fit), not replicate measurements, so they cannot establish a true noise floor. Open Targets locus-to-gene already reports a calibrated score.

models_beatable.why: The relevant comparators are not beatable in the usual sense: PLEIO, PolarMorphism and FactorGo are association tests and factor models with no held-out predictive number, and Open Targets locus-to-gene (2021, gradient boosting, nested cross-validation, calibrated output) solves a different, better-labelled task.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on two conditions: the existing tools are not predictors that can serve as a baseline on the same metric, and the natural added data (other GWAS summary statistics at the same variant) are the very quantities the label is computed from, so adding them is leakage rather than improvement.

ml_idea: Rejected idea, recorded for the file: embed GRCh37 sequence windows around each lead variant with a DNA language model (DNABERT-2 or Nucleotide Transformer), freeze the backbone, and fit a head to predict which of the four depression-disease liability factors a locus belongs to, or to rank variants by factor Z statistic against allele-frequency and gene-density baselines, with chromosome-level held-out splits and the major histocompatibility complex as positive control.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: a ranged GET showed ~8,287 variant rows per 400 KB compressed, so one 300 MB file is roughly 6-7 million rows and 1.5-2.5 GB uncompressed, streamable in chunks. The 30 hours is dominated by assembling features that are absent from the released files - reference genome extraction, GRCh37-to-GRCh38 liftover, and a linkage-disequilibrium block definition.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count how many of the 1,019 loci fall in distinct linkage-disequilibrium blocks and how many are shared between factors; if the four factor loci sets largely overlap, the four-class problem collapses and there is nothing left to predict.

verdict_reason: The released files are label-only: every predictor would have to be fetched from elsewhere, and the label is itself the output of a structural equation model fitted to other public GWAS, so the most natural features reconstruct it exactly. The usable unit count collapses from 6.8 million variants to 1,019 loci, the remaining task (predicting complex-trait association from DNA sequence) is crowded and known-hard, and no one would change an experiment on the result (Part I scored 3/8, C 4/10).
